content: The administration of drugs that increase gastric pH can lead to premature dissolution of budesonide products, potentially altering their release properties and absorption in the duodenum. Butabarbital may reduce the levels or effects of lansoprazole by influencing hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. This interaction is considered minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. Butalbital may also decrease the levels or effects of lansoprazole through a similar mechanism involving CYP2C19 metabolism. Again, this is a minor interaction with unknown significance. Lansoprazole can increase the levels or effects of cannabidiol by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Close monitoring is recommended, and therapy adjustments may be necessary. Conversely, cannabidiol can increase the levels or effects of lansoprazole via the same metabolic pathway. Dose reductions of sensitive CYP2C19 substrates should be considered when co-administered with cannabidiol. Lansoprazole may reduce the effects of capecitabine through an unknown mechanism. Retrospective data suggest that elevated gastric pH caused by proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) may impair the dissolution and/or absorption of capecitabine tablets. Close monitoring is advised. Carbamazepine can decrease the levels or effects of lansoprazole by affecting both hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism, as well as CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. Lansoprazole may reduce the levels or effects of carbonyl iron by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. Cenobamate can decrease the levels or effects of lansoprazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, while it may also increase the levels or effects of lansoprazole via CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. Dose reductions of CYP2C19 substrates should be considered when co-administered with cenobamate. Clarithromycin can increase the levels or effects of lansoprazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Lansoprazole may increase the levels or effects of clobazam by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Dosage adjustments may be required, as CYP2C19 inhibitors can increase exposure to N-desmethylclobazam, the active metabolite of clobazam. Close monitoring is recommended. Lansoprazole may reduce the effects of clopidogrel by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. The mean area under the curve (AUC) of clopidogrel’s active metabolite was reduced by approximately 14% when co-administered with lansoprazole in healthy subjects who were extensive CYP2C19 metabolizers. This reduction may impair clopidogrel’s efficacy, as its antiplatelet activity depends entirely on its active metabolite. Close monitoring is advised. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of lansoprazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Conivaptan can increase the levels or effects of lansoprazole via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Lansoprazole may decrease the levels of crizotinib by increasing gastric pH, which can reduce its solubility and bioavailability. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. No formal studies have been conducted, but caution and monitoring are recommended. Lansoprazole may decrease the levels of cyanocobalamin (vitamin B12) by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. Cyclophosphamide may increase the levels or effects of lansoprazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Dabrafenib can decrease the levels or effects of lansoprazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, while lansoprazole may reduce the levels or effects of dabrafenib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Drugs that alter upper gastrointestinal pH, such as PPIs, H2-blockers, and antacids, may reduce dabrafenib solubility and bioavailability. Caution and monitoring are advised. Lansoprazole may increase the levels or effects of dacomitinib through an unspecified mechanism. Concomitant use with PPIs decreases dacomitinib concentrations, potentially reducing its efficacy. PPIs should be avoided with dacomitinib. Alternatives such as locally-acting antacids or H2-receptor antagonists may be used, with specific timing considerations for administration. Danazol may increase the levels or effects of lansoprazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Lansoprazole may reduce the levels or effects of dapsone by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Alternative drugs should be considered. Darifenacin may decrease the effectiveness of lansoprazole through a theoretical mechanism involving other antisecretory agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Lansoprazole may reduce the levels or effects of dasatinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Dasatinib may also increase lansoprazole levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Devil’s claw may reduce the effects of lansoprazole through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Dexamethasone may decrease the levels or effects of lansoprazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Lansoprazole may increase the levels or effects of diazepam (both buccal and intranasal forms) by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Strong or moderate CYP2C19 inhibitors may decrease the rate of diazepam elimination, increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Close monitoring is recommended. Lansoprazole may increase the toxicity of digoxin through an unspecified mechanism. It may also increase digoxin levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Alternative drugs should be considered. Dronedarone may increase the levels or effects of lansoprazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of lansoprazole via CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Efavirenz may decrease the levels or effects of lansoprazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, while it may also increase lansoprazole levels via CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Elagolix may increase the levels or effects of lansoprazole by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism and decrease its levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Elagolix is a weak CYP2C19 inhibitor and a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF (components of Stribild) do not exhibit clinically significant interactions with PPIs based on drug interaction studies. Close monitoring is still advised. Encorafenib may both inhibit and induce CYP3A4 at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. Co-administration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may increase toxicity or reduce efficacy. Caution and monitoring are advised. Enzalutamide may decrease the levels or effects of lansoprazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered. Lansoprazole may reduce the levels of erlotinib by altering its solubility and bioavailability through changes in upper gastrointestinal pH. Concomitant use of PPIs with erlotinib should be avoided if possible. Erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, and stearate forms) may increase the levels or effects of lansoprazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Eslcarbazepine acetate may increase the levels or effects of lansoprazole by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Etravirine may decrease the levels or effects of lansoprazole via CYP3A4 metabolism, while it may also increase lansoprazole levels via CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Fedratinib may increase the levels or effects of lansoprazole by affecting both CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Co-administration with dual CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 inhibitors should be avoided.
